Buying guide / Using building height

Mezzanine floor vs multi-tier shelving

Both use the height of your building. A mezzanine floor is an independent structural steel floor that creates open space for storage, offices, packing or assembly, designed for floor loads from 350 kg/m² to 2,000 kg/m² and more. Multi-tier shelving builds 2 to 4 picking levels into the shelving itself, with walkways between the shelves, and suits hand-picking of small items.

Which one fits your warehouse?

  • Choose a mezzanine floor when you need open floor area that can change use over time, carry heavy loads or host offices, packing stations or machinery.
  • Choose multi-tier shelving when the upper levels are only for picking many small SKUs by hand and you want storage and access in one structure.
  • Combine them when you need both: shelving on a mezzanine floor, or pallet racking below a rack-supported mezzanine.

Safety and approvals

Both systems are designed with stairs, handrails, gates and toe boards, and sprinkler integration is coordinated with the building fire design. Requirements for approvals vary by state and building use, so check with your local authority and fire consultant early. ProRack prepares the structural design and drawings in Tekla Structures and RSTAB as part of the project.

Questions

Frequently asked questions

Is a mezzanine floor or multi-tier shelving better for picking?

Multi-tier shelving is usually better for hand-picking many small items, because the shelving and walkways form picking aisles on 2 to 4 levels. A mezzanine floor is better when the upper level needs open space for storage, offices, packing or assembly.

How much load can a mezzanine floor carry?

ProRack mezzanine floors are designed for floor loads from 350 kg/m² to 2,000 kg/m² and more. The design load is set from the intended use and confirmed in the structural design.

Can multi-tier shelving be built on a mezzanine?

Yes. Shelving can be installed on a mezzanine floor, and pallet racking can sit below a rack-supported mezzanine. The structure is designed for the combined loads.
